instruction:
Task background: The internal Acme Todo single-page app (Dexie + IndexedDB v3) started exhibiting a set of **vague** rendering symptoms after a failed migration: "Today's high-priority items" is missing one row; one row in the "All todos by project" table shows project name as `?`; one row's Due column displays `Invalid Date`. The HTML returned by `http://localhost:7110/` is purely a static shell — eyeballing the source reveals nothing — **all symptoms originate from dirty data the frontend reads out of IndexedDB**: the affected fields are the runtime JS type of values (`priority` should be a number but is stored as a string), the foreign key `projectId` pointing to a non-existent project, and a non-numeric `dueAt`. The "actual JS types of values + the key tuples actually indexed by the compound index" can only be seen when expanding the `AcmeTodoDB` tree in the browser storage viewer; HAR / HTML / `curl` carry no such semantic information.

Ready-to-use scene materials:
- App under test: `http://localhost:7110/` (warmup auto-starts an Express server serving the static SPA + Dexie 4.0.7 library from `/tmp_workspace/app/`; `/healthz` for liveness probe).
- IndexedDB database: `AcmeTodoDB`, containing the `todos` object store (12 rows, at least 3 rows exhibit more than two of the three aforementioned corruption classes), the `projects` object store (4 rows, id 1..4), and the `[projectId+priority]` compound index.
- Frontend source: `/tmp_workspace/app/public/js/seed.js` + `app.js` (**modification forbidden** — this task is data-layer repair, not code repair; SHA-256 is compared against the original `setup/` image).
- helper: `/tmp_workspace/app/playwright_dump.js`, which visits `http://127.0.0.1:7110/`, waits for seed completion, then uses `page.evaluate` to dump both tables fully to `/tmp_workspace/results/idb_dump_<tag>.json` (`tag` specified via call argument). The agent may reuse it directly or rewrite it.

Goal: Locate ≥ 3 corrupted rows covering at least 2 corruption categories, **fix the data to the correct state by writing only to IndexedDB** (do not modify frontend source, do not delete and rebuild the database), and leave behind a forensic chain that a third party can independently audit. How you spin up the browser, expand the storage viewer, and drive the IndexedDB repair (Playwright / CDP / custom script — any approach works) is up to you.

The following deliverables must be produced under `/tmp_workspace/results/`:

1. **Static SSR baseline** `page_static.html`: a copy of the HTML text returned by the `/` path of the app under test (≥ 200 bytes). This file must **not** contain any of the keywords `Invalid Date` / `Infinity` / `corrupt` — this proves the symptoms come from runtime data read out of IndexedDB rather than from the SSR HTML.

2. **Pre-repair full IndexedDB snapshot** `idb_dump_before.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "todos":    [{"id": <int>, "title": ..., "priority": ..., "projectId": ..., "dueAt": ..., ...}, ... 12 rows total ...],
     "projects": [{"id": <int>, "name": ...}, ... ≥ 4 rows ...]
   }
   ```
   Field values must preserve the original JS types of the source data — corrupt-class string `"high"`, `projectId` value `99`, string `"Infinity"`, etc., must appear as-is, so that all three corruption classes are detectable from the dump.

3. **Corruption diagnosis** `corruption_report.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "corrupted_rows": [
       {"id": <int>, "kind": "<kind>", "field": "<field>", "bad_value": <as-is>},
       ... ≥ 3 entries ...
     ],
     "evidence_screenshots": ["<.png filename>", ...]
   }
   ```
   `kind` is drawn from the set `{priority_type, dangling_project, due_at_invalid}` and must **cover at least 2 kinds**; at least 3 `id`s must hit real corrupted rows.

4. **Repair script** `repair.js`: ≥ 200 bytes of valid JS. Requirements:
   - Must write IndexedDB in the same-origin context of an already-loaded page (via any of `page.evaluate` / `evaluateHandle` / direct use of Dexie's same-origin API);
   - Must **never** contain `indexedDB.deleteDatabase` / `rm -rf` / invoking `rm` via `child_process`, or any other "delete-and-rebuild" or file-level destructive path;
   - Repair semantics: every non-number `priority` is mapped to int (e.g. `"high"→1`, `"med"→2`, `"low"→3`); rows pointing at a non-existent project either gain a placeholder project (e.g. `{id:99, name:"Recovered project 99"}`) or are migrated to Inbox (`projectId=1`) — pick one of the two; non-numeric `dueAt` is replaced with a valid epoch ms.

5. **Repair script run log** `repair.log`: the combined stdout/stderr log from running `repair.js`; must include a line with the marker `REPAIR_OK <number_of_rows_repaired>`.

6. **Post-repair full IndexedDB snapshot** `idb_dump_after.json`: same schema as `idb_dump_before.json`. After repair, the following must hold: `todos` still has 12 rows (database not dropped, no rows lost); every row's `priority` is a number; every row's `dueAt` is a number; every row's `projectId` resolves to an existing `id` in the `projects` table.

7. **Visual forensic screenshots** (each ≥ 4 KB, taken from the actual rendered state):
   - `view_app_glitch.png`: pre-repair app page. Must simultaneously show the Today's high-priority / All todos by project / Health sections, and at least one table row must carry a visible "bad row" marker (pink-background `.bad` class highlight) or explicitly render `?` as the project name / `Invalid Date` as the Due value.
   - `view_idb_todos_store.png`: the key/value view of the `AcmeTodoDB → todos` object store in the browser storage viewer, with at least one row expanded into a JSON tree, from which the `priority` field can be read as a quoted string (e.g. `"high"`) or the `dueAt` field as the string `"Infinity"` or some other anomalous JS type — this kind of type color/marker is only directly visible in that viewer's rendering.
   - `view_idb_compound_index.png`: the `[projectId+priority]` compound index view of the same database. Multiple key tuple entries (e.g. `[2,1]`, `[2,3]`) are visible, and it can be verified that the row whose priority is the string `[2,"high"]` is **not** indexed (this is precisely the root cause of "high-priority items is missing one row").
   - `view_idb_projects_store.png`: the `projects` object store view, from which the 4 rows with id 1..4 can be counted (no project with id=99 exists, forming a dangling relationship with the row in `todos` whose `projectId=99`).
   - `view_app_after.png`: the app page after repair and refresh. In the Health section, `hot_via_index` should equal 5 (was 4 before repair); no table row carries the `.bad` pink background any longer; the table no longer shows `Invalid Date` or `?` project names.
   - `view_idb_index_after.png`: the `[projectId+priority]` compound index view after re-verification, showing 5 key tuples of the form `[<projectId>, 1]` (was 4 before repair), proving that the row previously dropped due to a string-typed priority is now indexed.

8. **Final report** `findings.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "rows_before": 12,
     "rows_after": 12,
     "corrupted_count_before": <int>,
     "corrupted_count_after": 0,
     "hot_via_index_before": <int>,
     "hot_via_index_after": 5,
     "kinds_seen": ["priority_type", "dangling_project", "due_at_invalid"],
     "fix_strategy": {
       "priority_type":     "string→int",
       "dangling_project":  "create-placeholder | migrate-to-inbox",
       "due_at_invalid":    "replace-with-epoch-ms"
     },
     "evidence_screenshots": [
       "view_app_glitch.png", "view_idb_todos_store.png", "view_idb_compound_index.png",
       "view_idb_projects_store.png", "view_app_after.png", "view_idb_index_after.png"
     ]
   }
   ```

Hard constraints:
- The SHA-256 of `app/public/js/seed.js` and `app/public/js/app.js` must match the originals in `setup/` (any source-code change drops the fixture-integrity gate to 0).
- The `todos` row count is strictly = 12 both before and after repair; bypassing repair via delete-and-rebuild is not allowed.
- In the report, `hot_via_index_after` must be 5 and `corrupted_count_after` must be 0.

parameters.warmup:
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/state /opt/web11_gt && chmod 777 /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/state
if [ -f /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json ]; then
  mv /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json /opt/web11_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || cp /tmp_workspace/gt/expected.json /opt/web11_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || true
  chown -R root:root /opt/web11_gt 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 700 /opt/web11_gt 2>/dev/null || true
  chmod 600 /opt/web11_gt/expected.json 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf /tmp_workspace/gt 2>/dev/null || true
fi
which curl || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing curl ca-certificates && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which jq || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing jq && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which node || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing nodejs npm && break; sleep 5; done) || true
which tesseract || (for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq --fix-missing tesseract-ocr fonts-noto-cjk && break; sleep 5; done) || true
pip3 install --break-system-packages --ignore-installed --quiet blinker 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --ignore-installed --quiet blinker || true
pip3 install --break-system-packages --quiet pillow pytesseract requests playwright 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --quiet pillow pytesseract requests playwright || true
PWB="chro""mium"
python3 -m playwright install "$PWB" >/tmp/pw_install.log 2>&1 || true
cd /tmp_workspace && timeout 240 npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund express@4.19.2 playwright@1.44.1 || true
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace/public/js
test -f /tmp_workspace/public/js/dexie.min.js || curl -fsSL --retry 5 --max-time 60 -o /tmp_workspace/public/js/dexie.min.js https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dexie@4.0.7/dist/dexie.min.js || true
cd /tmp_workspace && nohup node server.js >/tmp/start.log 2>&1 & sleep 3; for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -sf http://localhost:7110/healthz >/dev/null && break; sleep 1; done
